newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat rises on EU tender award.
newsitem.headline: French wheat rises on EU tender award.

text.p: French wheat prices firmed on Friday after the European Union granted more wheat than most exporters had hoped for at its auction on Thursday, dealers said.
Sales of French wheat to Algeria and Morocco and hopes of further business with Iraq were also supportive.
Firmer prices in turn kept sellers sidelined, they said.
January wheat into Rouen was offered at 865 francs per tonne, up 7.5 francs from Thursday, excluding carrying charges.
Rouen wheat for February delivery fetched 860 francs per tonne, up five francs on the previous day.
On Thursday the European Union released 343,100 tonnes of soft wheat at a maximum rebate of 14.90 Ecus per tonne.
Traders said the refund was higher than expected, an indication the Commission was willing to push exports.
"Brussels did well yesterday. We cannot complain," one exporter for a leading trade house said.
"The Commission was in a position to give less (a lower refund). It wants to sell. That is encouraging," another exporter said.
The Commission could have exported its wheat at a lower refund because of the firmer dollar.
Instead it chose to slightly raise the refund on wheat to 14.90 Ecus per tonne from the 14.67 awarded the previous week.
Exporters were still awaiting news of a tender Iraq launched for the purchase of French wheat.
There was market speculation Iraq may have bought more than the 100,000 tonnes it had tendered for. But there has been no official confirmation of any deals so far.
